chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who kissed his wife while he was in the state of Ihram (for Hajj or Umrah). He said: 'Upon him is a camel (as expiation), even if he did not ejaculate, and he is not permitted to eat from it.'
And whoever played with his wife until he ejaculated, upon both of them is the expiation. Narrated.

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: The expiation or penalty for a religious violation
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel used as a specific form of expiation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram, a sacred state for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man in Ihram who kisses or has intimacy with his wife?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the graduated severity of expiations (kaffarah) for violations of Ihram restrictions, distinguishing between minor acts like kissing and major acts like sexual intercourse. The requirement of a 'badanah' (a mature camel) for kissing, even without ejaculation, underscores the sanctity of the sacred state, while the joint liability for both spouses in cases of full intimacy highlights the shared responsibility in ritual purity. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for understanding the proportionality of penalties relative to the degree of intimacy during Hajj or Umrah.
